rows: You can now sign in to Kiwi
The subject says what happened and what the reader can do; "granted" is the system's word.

rows.t: The browser preview's header: no exclamation mark, and the name from branding (C17). brandLabel is "{institutionName} Kiwi" when an institution name is configured and "Kiwi" when it is not (the rule of `BRAND_LABEL` in `src/config/branding.ts`: an unbranded deployment never reads "Kiwi Kiwi"); the browser preview and the backend mail apply the same rule, the backend to its `INSTITUTION_NAME`.

The backend header, and the first line of the plain-text version, which has no header block (`email.templates.ts:255`, `:278`): no exclamation mark; the same words and rule as EM.11. brandLabel is "{institutionName} Kiwi" when an institution name is configured and "Kiwi" when it is not (the rule of `BRAND_LABEL` in `src/config/branding.ts`: an unbranded deployment never reads "Kiwi Kiwi"); the browser preview and the backend mail apply the same rule, the backend to its `INSTITUTION_NAME`.

The HTML paragraph repeated the header word for word (`:258`), so the HTML loses it. The plain-text version has no header block: its line `Welcome to …` (`:278`) is its heading, so it stays and takes EM.12's wording.

rows: The email goes to anyone granted access, not only students, and "Dear" is formal for a product notice.

rows.o: You have been granted access to Kiwi as per your request. You can now log in from the website.
rows.n: You can now sign in to Kiwi with the email address this message was sent to.
rows.t: "As per your request" is a claim the product cannot back; the sentence says what changed and how to use it. It makes no claim about when the account is created. An earlier draft added "If you haven't signed in before, Kiwi sets up your account the first time you do", which is false for a recipient whose account an administrator created with a password: the System email page sends this template to any user the administrator selects (`email.controller.ts:392-421`, `email.service.ts:254`), and an administrator-created password account exists from the moment the administrator submits the form (`auth.controller.ts:51-60` and `auth.service.ts:145-186`: `registerUser` creates the user, its allowlist entry and its enrollments at once). The first sentence holds for every recipient: a pending user signs in with Google, a password account with its password.

rows: The link's text says where it goes (Redish); it is the link on the welcome email, and in the plain-text version the address follows "Sign in at".

rows.o: You have been added to {className} on Kiwi.
rows.n: You've been added to {className}{ ({professorName})} on Kiwi.
rows.t: A contraction in the same quiet voice. The parenthesis after the class name is kept: the source writes it only when the instructor's name is set (`professorName ? ... : ''`, `email.templates.ts:96` and `:120`), so the part in the second braces is left out when the name is not set, and the spec's email table quotes this exact string. The dialog's prefilled message uses the sentence without that part (A-16.43): the dialog does not know the name.
